task.title: RETURNS
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Customer service handles returns by hand, and the refund endpoint, POST /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/refund, does nothing. Build returns and refunds for orders.

Admin API (protected like the other /api/v1/private endpoints, for the store given by ?store=):

- POST /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/returns records a return and refunds it. The body is {"lines": [{"sku": "...", "quantity": 2}], "restock": true, "reason": "..."}; "reason" is optional. It returns HTTP 201 with the return.
- GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/returns lists the order's returns, oldest first.
- POST /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/refund refunds everything on the order that has not been returned yet, as one return with "restock" false and reason "refund", and returns HTTP 201 with that return.
- A return is JSON: {"id": 7, "orderId": 12, "lines": [{"sku": "...", "quantity": 2, "amount": 50.00}], "tax": 6.50, "amount": 56.50, "restocked": true, "reason": "...", "date": "2026-11-04"}. "amount" on a line is what the customer paid for those units; "tax" is the tax refunded; "amount" on the return is the lines plus the tax.

Rules:

- An order that does not exist in the store gives HTTP 404 Not Found. A CANCELED or REFUNDED order cannot be returned or refunded: HTTP 409 Conflict.
- Each line's sku must be a product on the order and its quantity more than 0, and the request must have at least one line; otherwise HTTP 400 Bad Request. Lines with the same sku in one request count together. A product can't be returned more times in total than it was ordered: a request that would go over gives HTTP 400 and records nothing.
- A line's amount is the unit price the customer paid on the order, times the quantity.
- Tax: the order's tax (the sum of its tax lines) is shared across its products in proportion to their subtotals. A return refunds the tax on what it returns: the order's tax times the returned amount divided by the order's products subtotal, rounded to 2 decimal places, halves rounding up. The return that completes the order (after it, every unit has been returned) refunds exactly the tax not refunded yet, so that the tax refunded always adds up to the order's tax.
- With "restock" true, each returned product's stock goes up by the quantity returned. With false, stock is unchanged.
- When every unit of the order has been returned, the order's status becomes REFUNDED. Until then it keeps its status.
- Every return adds an entry to the order's status history (GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/history), with the order's status after the return and a comment that names the amount refunded.
- Every return is recorded as a REFUND payment transaction for its amount, listed by GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/payment/transactions.
- The order, whenever it is returned by GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}, has a line in "totals" with code "order.total.refunded" and the total refunded so far as a positive "value", once anything has been refunded. Its other totals don't change.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

runs.report:
## Scope and classification

Implementation task for the shopizer Maven multi-module repository. No linked GitHub issue or prior implementation was supplied or found in the checkout. The work should proceed to Implement; no separate design approval is required because the requested API, validation, accounting, inventory, history, and status behavior are explicit.

## Evidence

- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/order/OrderPaymentApi.java:335-343` defines `POST /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/refund`, but `refundPayment` returns `null` and currently responds 200.
- The same controller authorizes private payment transaction reads for the store and admin groups at `:204-221`; new return/refund routes should use the same `AuthorizationUtils` groups and `?store` resolution.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/order/OrderApi.java:263-280` is the existing private order lookup route. It delegates to the order facade; store-scoped lookup and missing-order handling must be preserved.
- `sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/order/orderproduct/OrderProduct.java:34-44` stores the order SKU, ordered quantity, and paid one-time charge needed for return validation and line amounts.
- `sm-core-model` already has `OrderStatus.REFUNDED` and `CANCELED`; `Order` persists order products, totals, and ordered status history.
- `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/payments/PaymentServiceImpl.java:518-565` has an existing gateway-oriented refund flow, but it creates a transaction through the payment module, subtracts the order total, always marks the order REFUNDED, and adds history. That behavior does not satisfy partial returns or the requirement that other order totals remain unchanged, so it should not be reused unchanged.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/populator/order/ReadableOrderPopulator.java:135-192` builds the public `totals` list from persisted order totals. A persisted refund total with the required code can therefore be exposed without changing the existing total, tax, shipping, or subtotal entries, subject to the required positive value and code.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/order/OrderPaymentApi.java:204-221` and the facade implementation at `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/order/facade/OrderFacadeImpl.java:1599-1619` already expose persisted payment transactions, including `TransactionType.REFUND`.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/order/OrderStatusHistoryApi.java:37-56` exposes existing order history, and `OrderFacadeImpl.java:1432-1455` maps persisted history in insertion order.
- Inventory is represented by product availabilities; existing decrement logic in `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/order/OrderServiceImpl.java:190-210` updates availability quantities and persists the product. Return restocking should use the corresponding availability service/update path.
- Existing integration coverage includes `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/order/OrderApiIntegrationTest.java`, but no return/refund tests were found.

## Problem and proposed scope

Add a return domain model and persistence mapping for return headers and return lines, request/response DTOs, service/facade operations, and private v1 controller routes:

1. `POST /private/orders/{id}/returns`, HTTP 201.
2. `GET /private/orders/{id}/returns`, oldest first.
3. Change the existing `POST /private/orders/{id}/refund` to create one residual return with `restock=false` and reason `refund`, HTTP 201, returning the return representation rather than a payment transaction.

The return operation should run transactionally: resolve the order by id and merchant store; reject missing orders with 404 and CANCELED/REFUNDED orders with 409; normalize duplicate request SKUs before validation; reject empty, unknown, nonpositive, or over-return quantities with 400 before persisting or mutating anything; calculate paid line amounts from `OrderProduct.oneTimeCharge`; calculate proportional tax from persisted TAX totals and product subtotal, rounded HALF_UP to two decimals; on the final return assign the remaining unrefunded tax to eliminate rounding drift; optionally increment product availability; create a REFUND transaction for the return amount; append status history using the post-return status and a comment naming the amount; persist cumulative positive `order.total.refunded`; and set order status REFUNDED only when all units have been returned.

The refund-all operation should compute all residual quantities, reject a canceled/refunded order, and follow the same atomic return path. If no residual units remain, the explicit requirements do not define whether this is 409, 400, or an empty return; implementation should use the repository's established exception conventions or raise this only if tests/spec clarification exposes a needed choice.

## Likely affected components

- `sm-core-model`: new return/return-line entities and any enum/constants needed for return persistence.
- `sm-core`: repositories and a transactional return/refund service; payment transaction creation; status history and order-total updates; product availability restock.
- `sm-shop-model`: persistable return request, readable return, and readable line DTOs.
- `sm-shop`: v1 returns API/controller, facade methods, mapping/population, replacement of the no-op refund endpoint, and HTTP exception mapping for 400/404/409.
- Database schema/migration resources if this repository's schema convention requires explicit table definitions.
- `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/order`: authenticated, store-scoped endpoint coverage; focused service tests for validation, tax rounding, final-return remainder, duplicate SKUs, atomic failure, restock, history, transaction, totals, and status transitions.

## Acceptance checks

- Private routes require the same admin authorization groups and honor `?store`; an order id belonging to another store behaves as not found.
- Create returns responds 201 with id, orderId, lines, tax, amount, restocked, reason, and date; list returns is oldest first.
- Missing order is 404; CANCELED or REFUNDED is 409; malformed/empty/unknown/nonpositive/over-limit requests are 400 and leave order, stock, totals, history, transactions, and return rows unchanged.
- Duplicate SKUs are aggregated for validation and output behavior is deterministic.
- Each line amount equals the paid unit charge multiplied by returned quantity; return amount equals lines plus tax.
- Tax uses the sum of order TAX lines, proportional to returned product subtotal, HALF_UP to two decimals, with the final return receiving exactly the remaining tax.
- `restock=true` increments each returned product's stock; false does not.
- Partial returns preserve the existing order status; a fully returned order becomes REFUNDED.
- Each return adds history with the resulting status and a comment naming the refunded amount, and adds one REFUND transaction for that amount.
- GET order adds exactly the cumulative positive `order.total.refunded` entry after any refund, while all other totals remain unchanged.
- POST refund creates a single residual return with all outstanding units, `restock=false`, reason `refund`, and HTTP 201.

## Assumptions and risks

- “Recorded as a REFUND payment transaction” is treated as an internal ledger transaction requirement; the existing gateway `PaymentService.processRefund` is unsuitable for partial/multiple returns because it invokes configured gateways and changes the order total.
- Return records are assumed to require durable persistence because GET listing and cumulative accounting must survive subsequent requests.
- The requirements do not specify behavior for refund-all after every unit is already returned, nor exact error payload shapes; follow existing exception handlers and tests unless product direction is required.
- Concurrency can otherwise allow two requests to over-return the same units; the service should use a transaction and appropriate locking/serialization around the order and return quantity calculation.

## Complexity

High. This crosses API, DTO, persistence/schema, transactional service, payment ledger, inventory, order totals, status history, and integration tests, with monetary rounding and atomicity requirements. Estimated implementation size is medium-to-large across `sm-core-model`, `sm-core`, `sm-shop-model`, and `sm-shop`.

Admin API (protected like the other /api/v1/private endpoints, for the store given by ?store=):

- POST /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/returns records a return and refunds it. The body is {"lines": [{"sku": "...", "quantity": 2}], "restock": true, "reason": "..."}; "reason" is optional. It returns HTTP 201 with the return.
- GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/returns lists the order's returns, oldest first.
- POST /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/refund refunds everything on the order that has not been returned yet, as one return with "restock" false and reason "refund", and returns HTTP 201 with that return.
- A return is JSON: {"id": 7, "orderId": 12, "lines": [{"sku": "...", "quantity": 2, "amount": 50.00}], "tax": 6.50, "amount": 56.50, "restocked": true, "reason": "...", "date": "2026-11-04"}. "amount" on a line is what the customer paid for those units; "tax" is the tax refunded; "amount" on the return is the lines plus the tax.

Rules:

- An order that does not exist in the store gives HTTP 404 Not Found. A CANCELED or REFUNDED order cannot be returned or refunded: HTTP 409 Conflict.
- Each line's sku must be a product on the order and its quantity more than 0, and the request must have at least one line; otherwise HTTP 400 Bad Request. Lines with the same sku in one request count together. A product can't be returned more times in total than it was ordered: a request that would go over gives HTTP 400 and records nothing.
- A line's amount is the unit price the customer paid on the order, times the quantity.
- Tax: the order's tax (the sum of its tax lines) is shared across its products in proportion to their subtotals. A return refunds the tax on what it returns: the order's tax times the returned amount divided by the order's products subtotal, rounded to 2 decimal places, halves rounding up. The return that completes the order (after it, every unit has been returned) refunds exactly the tax not refunded yet, so that the tax refunded always adds up to the order's tax.
- With "restock" true, each returned product's stock goes up by the quantity returned. With false, stock is unchanged.
- When every unit of the order has been returned, the order's status becomes REFUNDED. Until then it keeps its status.
- Every return adds an entry to the order's status history (GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/history), with the order's status after the return and a comment that names the amount refunded.
- Every return is recorded as a REFUND payment transaction for its amount, listed by GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/payment/transactions.
- The order, whenever it is returned by GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}, has a line in "totals" with code "order.total.refunded" and the total refunded so far as a positive "value", once anything has been refunded. Its other totals don't change.
